title: Datadog Application key (legacy 40-hex): one-property twin (context)
summary: 8 inputs are identical to a positive input except for one change: the value is unchanged but the carrier lacks the marker that makes the value identifiable. Legacy mutation notes: context: the DATADOG_APP_KEY constant renamed BUILD_REVISION, a commit pin; the value is unchanged, context: the DATADOG_APP_KEY constant renamed EXPECTED_SHA1, a download checksum; the datadog import stays two lines above; the value is unchanged, and context: the DD-APPLICATION-KEY header name replaced by X-Content-SHA1, a body checksum header; the Datadog host stays two lines above; the value is unchanged, and 5 more. Twin of "Datadog Application key (legacy 40-hex): must be flagged".
rationale: A twin changes exactly one property, so the expected outcome differs from the positive for that one reason. Reporting the twin is a false alarm, and it shows that the changed property is part of what identifies the credential.

expectation.rationale: Negative twin of datadog-application-key-legacy-dotenv: context: the DD_APPLICATION_KEY name replaced by SOURCE_COMMIT, a deploy commit; DD_SITE stays on the line above; the value is unchanged. The value is unchanged and exactly one property of the assignment context differs; expected silence is project policy, as the positive's expectation is.
